```json
{
  "edition_title": "Keen Africa Opportunities Digest: September 2026 Edition",
  "edition_intro": "This month brings a tight window worth moving fast on: Oxford and UK scholarships closing within days, a Nigeria-based leadership conference filling up in Enugu, and a national pitch competition open only to student founders already running a business. You already build things; these just give you the runway. Pick what fits your work and apply before the doors close.",
  "opportunities": [
    {
      "category": "scholarships",
      "title": "Chevening Scholarships 2027/2028 (UK Master's)",
      "summary": "Fully funds a one-year master's degree at any UK university, covering tuition, flights, and a monthly living stipend.",
      "deadline": "6 October 2026",
      "eligibility": "Nigerian citizens with an undergraduate degree and at least 2,800 hours (roughly two years) of work experience",
      "apply_url": "https://www.chevening.org/scholarship/nigeria/",
      "body_md": "Chevening is the UK government's flagship global scholarship, funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office to build future leaders with ties to Britain. It covers full tuition, a monthly stipend, return flights, and additional grants for arrival, study materials, and travel within the UK, with no requirement to return home immediately after unlike some tied scholarships.\n\nCompetition is fierce: around 32 Nigerians made it through from over 11,000 applicants in a recent cycle, so the essays matter as much as the CV. Nigeria's eligibility can shift year to year, which makes this cycle worth applying to now rather than waiting for a future one."
    },
    {
      "category": "scholarships",
      "title": "Rhodes Scholarship for West Africa 2027 (Oxford)",
      "summary": "Fully funds postgraduate study at the University of Oxford, including tuition, a living stipend, airfare, and a settling-in allowance.",
      "deadline": "27 August 2026",
      "eligibility": "Citizens of West African countries including Nigeria, resident there for at least 5 of the last 10 years",
      "apply_url": "https://www.rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk/scholarships/applications/west-africa/",
      "body_md": "The Rhodes Scholarship is the oldest and among the most prestigious postgraduate awards in the world, run by Rhodes House at Oxford. The West Africa constituency covers 19 countries, and shortlisted candidates are invited to in-person interviews in their region before final selection, so this isn't a paper exercise, it's a real shot at one of the deepest alumni networks in global academia and public life.\n\nThis window is closing in days, not weeks, so it only belongs on this list for readers who can pull a strong application together immediately: transcripts, references, and a personal statement that shows leadership beyond the classroom. If that's you, don't wait for the next cycle."
    },
    {
      "category": "grants",
      "title": "Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation 2027",
      "summary": "Awards up to £50,000 plus a year of tailored business support to African innovators building scalable engineering solutions.",
      "deadline": "8 September 2026",
      "eligibility": "Lead applicant must be a citizen of a Sub-Saharan African country, applying individually or as a small team",
      "apply_url": "https://africaprize.raeng.org.uk/",
      "body_md": "Run by the UK's Royal Academy of Engineering, the Africa Prize is the continent's largest award dedicated purely to engineering innovation, not just an idea, but hardware, products, and systems that solve real local problems. Total prize money across the cohort is £85,000: £50,000 to the overall winner, £10,000 each to three finalists, and £5,000 for a One-to-Watch award.\n\nThe real value is the year of commercialisation support that comes before the prize money: mentoring, investment readiness training, and a network of engineers who've taken hardware ideas to market across the continent. Applications run in two stages, so getting the first-stage submission in early gives you room to strengthen it if you're shortlisted."
    },
    {
      "category": "conferences",
      "title": "Young African Leaders Conference (YALCON) 2026",
      "summary": "A free, one-day leadership and entrepreneurship conference in Enugu bringing 300+ young Africans together to pitch ideas and access post-conference mentorship.",
      "deadline": "1 September 2026",
      "eligibility": "Young Africans committed to leadership, entrepreneurship, or sustainable development; entry is free but registration is required",
      "apply_url": "https://yalcon-2026.vercel.app/",
      "body_md": "YALCON brings together young delegates from across Africa for a day of talks, pitching, and networking around this year's theme, 'From Idea to Global Impact.' It's a smaller, community-built event rather than a corporate summit, which means more direct access to organizers, speakers, and fellow delegates than you'd get at a large trade conference.\n\nSelected applicants get invited based on the leadership potential and social impact shown in their registration, and delegates who stand out are offered mentorship running from October through December after the conference. Registration is free, so the only cost is showing up in Enugu on 12 September ready to pitch."
    },
    {
      "category": "competitions",
      "title": "NANS Innovate 2026",
      "summary": "A national pitch competition for Nigerian student entrepreneurs, with the top 20 winning transparent funding to grow their existing businesses.",
      "deadline": "8 September 2026",
      "eligibility": "Currently enrolled Nigerian tertiary students already running a business, from any of the 36 states or the FCT",
      "apply_url": "https://grants.nanshq.org/apply",
      "body_md": "Organized by the National Association of Nigerian Students, NANSInnovate 2026 is built specifically for students who've already started something, not idea-stage pitches. You submit a business proposal (max 10 pages) showing what you've built and how funding would scale it, and the strongest entrants compete in a national pitch event for direct funding.\n\nThere's no entry fee at any stage, which sets it apart from many student competitions that charge for registration or mentorship add-ons. If you're a student already running a business on the side, this is a direct, low-friction shot at capital without giving up equity."
    },
    {
      "category": "certifications",
      "title": "Cisco Networking Academy (Skills for All)",
      "summary": "Free, self-paced courses in networking, cybersecurity, Python, and data science, with Cisco digital badges you can add to a CV immediately.",
      "deadline": "Rolling",
      "eligibility": "Open to anyone with a free Cisco Skills for All account; no prerequisites for foundation-level courses",
      "apply_url": "https://skillsforall.com/",
      "body_md": "Cisco's Skills for All platform hosts the same curriculum used in the CCNA pathway, starting with Introduction to Networks, alongside standalone courses in Linux, Python, IoT analytics, and cybersecurity fundamentals. Courses are self-paced and self-enroll, so there's no application to wait on, you start the day you sign up.\n\nIEEE Nigeria also runs a parallel collaboration with Cisco offering guided cohorts through the same foundation courses, useful if you'd rather learn alongside a group than solo. Either way, note that completing a free course earns a digital badge; the paid professional-level Cisco exams are a separate, later step if you want to go further."
    },
    {
      "category": "certifications",
      "title": "freeCodeCamp Certifications",
      "summary": "Free, project-based certifications in web development, data analysis, machine learning, and more, each backed by a real portfolio of built projects.",
      "deadline": "Rolling",
      "eligibility": "Open to anyone with internet access; no prior coding experience or application required",
      "apply_url": "https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn",
      "body_md": "freeCodeCamp is a nonprofit that has run entirely free, certification-backed coding curricula for over a decade, covering responsive web design, JavaScript algorithms, data analysis with Python, and machine learning, among others. Each certification requires you to build and ship real projects, not just pass quizzes, so what you walk away with is a portfolio, not just a badge.\n\nThere's no cohort to wait for and no acceptance process: you create a free account and start the curriculum immediately, working at your own pace. For anyone building toward a tech role without the budget for a bootcamp, it's one of the few free options with genuine industry recognition attached to the name."
    }
  ]
}
```
